wiki_text: In April 2026, PV Gas completed an upgrade of the operating Thi Vai LNG terminal's regasification capacity, raising throughput to about 288 tph (~9.5 million m3/day) from the originally designed ~171 tph, following commissioning trials on 18-19 March and 1-2 April 2026 (milestone reached 2 April 2026). PV Gas also stated it is investing to raise the terminal's nameplate from 1 mtpa to 3 mtpa by 2029 under Phase 2, and to deploy an FSRU at Vung Tau port between 2026 and 2029 with ~14 million Sm3/day of regasification capacity, bringing total system capacity to ~22 million Sm3/day. The 288 tph figure is an optimized/peak throughput and does not change the GEM nameplate capacity.

On 18 May 2026, a consortium of SK Innovation, PetroVietnam Power (PV Power) and NASU (an affiliate of TH Group) broke ground on the ~$2.3 billion Quynh Lap LNG project in Quynh Lap, Nghe An province (~220 km south of Hanoi), comprising a 1.5 GW combined-cycle gas turbine power plant and an LNG import terminal, with commercial operation targeted for December 2030. The project supersedes the earlier provincial investor-call stage at which GEM had recorded a placeholder owner.
